---

## The work

I am `reviewer`, the pull-request quality gate, working on **PR #450** (`atomaton/issue-449` → `main`), titled *"Separate a hand-off from a chain that continues elsewhere (#449)"*, opened by `engineer` (body ends `_Opened by [`engineer`](…runs/42071197152)_`). Issue #449: a merged PR filed its post-merge dispatch of the parent issue as `atomaton:ended=handoff`, so merged PRs read as "running" forever, making every close of a parent with merged children post a false "Runs were going on…" / `stop=requested` notice (measured on #443/#445/#446/#442).

The agreed policy (from the issue thread, fixed): separate `handoff` (this node held) from `chain_continues` (a run started elsewhere). Acceptance criteria: (1) merged PR no longer `ended=handoff` and `runInFlight(PR)` false; (2) closing a parent whose children are merged PRs emits neither "Runs were going on…" nor `stop=requested`; (3) an idle root's close notice must not say "an agent was working on it"; (4) tests pin this plus "genuinely running work is still stopped", using the fake `gh`. Version bump forbidden. `src/**` only; `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/atomaton-runtime/**` are generated (from `src/workflows/atomaton-runner.wac.ts`); `dist/` gitignored.

## Review state

- **Rounds so far: 1.** `get_pr_reviews` → `{"total":0}`, `list_pr_review_comments` → `{"total":0}`. Only this review round exists.
- **Checks on head:** all green (`atomaton-check`, `pull-request-checks (verify)`, `atomaton-tools`, `plan-*` success; `default-branch-checks` skipped by design).
- `get_pr_diff` was truncated at 30k; I fetched the rest via `https://api.github.com/repos/yuma-seno/atomaton/pulls/450/files?per_page=100&page=1..3` and read the working tree. Changed files: `src/adapters/github/thread.ts` + `.test.ts`, `src/adapters/github/work-tree.ts`, `src/domain/work/turn.ts` + `.test.ts`, `src/domain/work/completion-mention.ts` + `.test.ts`, `src/domain/work/closed-target.ts` + `.test.ts`, `src/entrypoints/machinery/decide_turn_ending.test.ts`, `src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.test.ts`, `src/entrypoints/machinery/stop_on_close.ts` + `.test.ts`, `src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/mcp.test.ts` (docstring only).
- Body claims: `bun run typecheck` exit 0, `bun test` 2196 pass / 0 fail / 6 skipped, `bun run synth` clean, `package.json` version untouched at 0.21.54 (verified in the tree).

## Verified sound

- `src/domain/work/turn.ts:239-247` — directive ⇒ `handed-off` (plus `continues` when a chain also continues); a dispatch elsewhere ⇒ `finished`/`no-report` + `continues: true`. `shouldReleaseGuard` (`turn.ts:270-273`) returns false for `continues`, preserving label behaviour. `nextToDispatch` unchanged.
- `src/adapters/github/thread.ts:461-475` — `runInFlight(repo, number, { merged })`: on `merged === true` only `shaped.holder === "agent"` (the `atomaton:took` claim) counts; the "coming" half (`whoseTurn(events) === "agent"`) is dropped. All call sites updated: `work-tree.ts:102-104,141,200,231` pass `merged` from `pull_request.merged_at` (readNode), `state === "MERGED"` (tag-search PR listing, consistent with `saysOpen`/`pullRequestOutcome` at `work-tree.ts:199,209`), and `false` for issues/links. `prune_atomaton_data.ts:131` deliberately keeps the wider answer (issues only).
- `src/domain/work/closed-target.ts:128-143` — `stopOnCloseNotice(number, running)`: idle receipt no longer claims "an agent was working on it", no "report here" promise. `stop_on_close.ts:66-79` — `stopOnCloseBody({number, rootRunning, closed, stopped})`, `STOP_TAG` only when `rootRunning` (from `all.find(n => n.number === root)?.running`, `stop_on_close.ts:124`).
- `completion-mention.ts:113` — `chainContinues || ending.continues` check moved above the `no-report` override, so a silent chain-continuing run stays silent (behaviour preserved, ordering now explicit).
- `.github/workflows/atomaton-runner.yml:1133,1216,1224,1243` — `post_result_comment` and `decide_turn_ending` both receive `--chain-continues`; the only readers of `turn-ending.outputs` are `should_release`, `dispatch_to`, `chain_over_to`. **`turn-ending.outputs.ended` is never read by any workflow step** (grep confirmed), so the runner/`.wac.ts` needed no change and the claimed "no `.wac.ts` edit needed" holds.
- No workflow/runner edit in the diff; no generated output edited; no `tools.servers`/agent-definition change; no version bump. `runInFlight` has exactly the one signature change, no external consumers outside `src`.

## Still open / to decide before writing the report

I had reached the end of the mandatory checks and was about to form the verdict and write the review. Candidate findings I was weighing (none yet written down):

1. **`stop_on_close.ts:127` early return.** `if (toStop.length === 0 && toClose.length === 0) { … return; }` — on a parent closed with only merged PRs, **no receipt comment is posted at all**. AC2 only requires silence about runs, so this is arguably fine, but it means the person who closed the issue gets nothing; the tests (`stop_on_close.test.ts:230-247`, `commented === []`) pin that empty output as intended. Decide whether this is a defect (loss of a receipt) or accepted.
2. **`requestStopAcross`** (`work-tree.ts:407-427`, used by `request_stop.ts`/`/stop`) has the same root-receipt shape but was not given the `rootRunning` treatment — `/stop` on a parent still writes an unconditional `STOP_TAG`. Out of #449's narrow scope, but note it.
3. **`releasesLabel`** (`run-report.ts:224-230`) still treats `ended=handoff` as "holds the label" and releases on `done`; after this change a merged PR ends `done`, so the crash-watch will release the label on it — consistent, since `shouldReleaseGuard` was changed the other way only for the dispatch path; worth one line, not a blocker.
4. **`endingOf` with both a directive and `chainContinues`** now carries `continues: true` on a `handed-off` (`turn.ts:239`), so `shouldReleaseGuard` (false anyway for `handed-off`) and `completion-mention` agree. No contradiction found.
5. **`work-tree.ts:199`** `const merged = !saysOpen(found.state) && found.state === "MERGED"` — the `!saysOpen(...)` conjunct is redundant (`"MERGED" !== "open"` always), a harmless redundancy worth at most a style note, not a blocker.
6. Nothing so far looks like a merge-blocking correctness defect; my leaning was **no defects**, then `check_merge_readiness(pull_number=450)` and, if ready, `merge_pr(pull_number=450)`.

## Rules to remember

- Report format: conclusion first; "How you know" anchored as `path:line`; "What you could not establish"; "What happens next". No opening/closing. Folds for evidence only.
- If merge-blocking defects: begin with `/<agent>` naming the body's `Opened by` agent — here `/engineer` — then list only evidenced defects (failing behaviour, location, correction).
- If no defects: call `check_merge_readiness(pull_number=450)` once, then act by the blocker table (`checks-*`, `conflicting`/`behind` → return to engineer for `merge_base_into_branch`, `merge-policy`/`human-authored`/`governance-change`/`merge-gate`/`blocked`/`draft`/`not-open` → report and end), else `merge_pr`.
- Never both a slash line and a person mention; @yuma-seno is the only callable person.

3. Root idle close → root notice doesn't say "an agent was working on it".
4. Tests for thread / stop_on_close / post_result_comment.

**A.** `runInFlight(repo, number, {merged:true})` returns `shaped.holder === "agent"`. For a merged PR: the thread after merge would be... The reviewer run claims (`took`), then posts result comment ending `done answers=<ask>` → claim closed, holder person. Good. But what about an old-style merged PR thread whose last event is `handed-off` and where the claim is closed by the handoff ending? Let's see: the MERGED_PR_HANDOFF_THREAD: `/engineer` (human, ask at 10), `took=10 run=5`, `ended=handoff answers=10`. Shaping: openClaim=10 at took; then ending answers=10 → closes claim (event handed-off != waiting) → openClaim undefined → holder person. So merged=true → false. Good.

But hold on — the `/engineer` comment by a human type User at id 10 was first, openClaim undefined then → kept. Fine.

**B.** Important: the shaper drops human comments made while openClaim set. Not relevant.

**C.** Stop-on-close: `rootRunning` computed and used to gate STOP_TAG. Previously the STOP_TAG was always written on root. Now only when root is running. But wait — is that a behavior degradation? The root's comment is posted by `commentOn(repo, root, rootBody)`. The STOP_TAG is what the running job polls for. If root isn't running, nothing polls. Fine.

But there's a subtlety: the root being closed means... hmm, not a degradation.

However: `nodesToStop(all)` includes root if root running, so `toStop.length===0` check would not return early when root runs. Fine.

**D.** But wait: `stopOnCloseBody`'s notice when root not running and a descendant IS running: `closedTheTreeNotice` says "Runs were going on #807" — test asserts. And the root receipt says "Nothing was running on it, so no run here had to be stopped." That's accurate.

**E.** Potential regression: In the stop_on_close script, the early return "Nothing is running under #root and nothing under it is open. Nothing to do." When a merged PR is the only child and root not running → no comment posted at all. Test asserts commented === []. Criterion 2 says neither "Runs were going on ..." nor stop=requested appear. OK. But is it a degradation to post no receipt at all when a person closes a parent issue with nothing under it? Previously the receipt was posted (they had stop tag). Hmm, previously `toStop` would include merged PRs (running true due to handoff) so it never returned early. Now returns early and posts nothing. Is that a "loss"? The person closing an issue gets no receipt. The issue says "no notice required" — criterion only says no false claims. It's arguably fine, and there's a test pinning it: "saying nothing about stopping runs, and does not ask anything to stop", expecting no comments. Hmm, but maybe a receipt would be better. Not a merge-blocking defect.

**F.** Bigger question: acceptance criterion 1 requires `runInFlight(PR)` false after merge+dispatch. With the tag now `done`, thread reads returned → whoseTurn person even without merged flag. Good.

**G.** Does anything break because `post_result_comment` now writes `ended=done` for a chain-continuing run on an OPEN node? Consider a run that dispatched a child … wait, that's `parked` (dispatch-elsewhere), not chainContinues. chainContinues is set when `"op":"dispatch"` appears in ops log. Where does `dispatch` op get logged for non-continuesChain? `dispatchRunner` logs `dispatch` when the target is the same node as the run (`here === d.number`) and continuesChain false. So a reload (`reload_environment`) on the same node logs `dispatch` → chain_continues=true → ending now `finished`+continues, tag `done`. But reload posts its own turn comment `ended=handoff` BEFORE dispatching, and then the run ends. Order: reload posts handoff comment (turn comment) then dispatches. Then post_result_comment runs? Actually reload ends the session via tool call; post_result_comment skips if the session ended with tool calls and appends footer to ending comment. So no second ending tag. The thread's newest ending stays handoff. Good.

But what about `dispatch_agent.ts` (the runner's Dispatch next agent step)? That's after post_result_comment; it passes `refusalEnding` not continuesChain. `dispatchAgent`... In that step, dispatch targets the same node, so op=dispatch → chain_continues... but that's after result comment, and the result comment already wrote handoff for the directive. Fine.

Now: does the `ended` change to `done` for chainContinues matter to `askSuperseded`? Look at `askSuperseded`: `answeredHere === "handed-off"` returns "handed-off". Previously for chainContinues the ending written was handoff; now done. Scenario: an ask is answered by an ending with `done` and answeredBy = agent (result comment has AGENT_TAG). `answeredHere === "returned"` → `own = answeredBy === "" || answeredBy === agent` → if dispatch agent same → "own-verdict". Previously "handed-off" → superseded. Both are non-undefined → superseded either way (`isAskSuperseded` presumably treats any defined as superseded). Fine.

A merged PR with a pending `asked` (dispatch marker) but no claim → not in flight.  * existed as six loose signals that three different places each derived their own
 * answer from — one of them in GitHub Actions expression syntax, where nothing
 * could test it.
 *

 * `domain/work/serialization-guard.ts` held one of those answers, and its header
 * recorded the same defect one level down: before it existed, the rule was
 * "a string-concatenated GitHub Actions `if:` expression inside
 * atomaton-runner.wac.ts (`REMOVE_LABEL_GUARD`) -- untestable, unnamed, and only
 * readable by parsing bash-adjacent expression syntax."

 * continue* from four of the same six signals, as an expression — and
 * `docs/work/how-it-works/what-keeps-two-runs-off-one-issue.md` forbids exactly
 * that, in a paragraph the expression sat beside.

 * name.

 *
 * Each is a different sentence a person says about a run that has stopped, and that
 * is the test applied: not "which flags were set" but "what would you tell somebody
 * who asked what happened".

export interface NextTurn {
  readonly agent: string;
}

 * How a turn ended.
 *
 * `spent` and `chain-over` are two different ceilings and are named apart because a
 * person goes and looks at different things: the first is this run reaching the
 * limit set on it, the second is a chain of runs going on too long without getting
 * anywhere. They were one `if:` condition away from being reported as each other.

 * as "completed" by everything downstream. It is not the same sentence: "it is done"
 * and "it ended and never said a word" are what a person would tell you about two very
 * different runs.

  /** The run itself did not complete. Nothing below it is known. */
  | "failed"
  /**
   * The repetition circuit breaker fired: the model got stuck repeating itself and
   * the completion was cut off.
   *
   * Named apart from `failed` because it is the one failure a person can act on. A
   * provider that hung up is nothing to look at; a run that looped is a run whose
   * turn can be asked again, and the person deciding whether to retry wants to know
   * which of the two they have.

  /** A person asked it to stop, and it did. */
  | "stopped"
  /** It reached the limit set on this run. */
  | "spent"
  /** The chain of runs reached ITS limit, so a named hand-off is refused rather than taken. */
  | "chain-over"
  /** Work continues: it named the next agent, or a tool call already started one. */
  | "handed-off"
  /**
   * The run ended inside a child-starting tool call: `launch_sub_agent` or
   * `create_pr` started work UNDER this node, and the session stopped there.
   *
   * Named apart from `handed-off` because the two hold the node differently: a
   * hand-off moves this node to the next agent, while a park leaves it held by
   * this run's own machinery until the children finish — the label stays on
   * (`shouldReleaseGuard`), and the aggregation re-invocation is the collection
   * of the parked turn, not a new one. See `domain/work/thread.ts`'s `waiting`.
   */
  | "parked"
  /**

   * words.
   *
   * Named so it cannot be read as a success, because it was being read as one.
   * Measured over 396 stored sessions: 39 ended without a line of closing text, and
   * three of those the core itself called `completed` — 313, 173 and 110 tool calls,

   * vocabulary had no word for it, so it fell into `finished` with the runs that
   * really had finished.
   */
  | "no-report"
  /** It is done, it said so, and nothing follows. */
  | "finished";

  readonly ended: Ending;
  /**
   * Who it named, when it named anybody.
   *
   * Present on `handed-off`, where it is dispatched, and on `chain-over`, where it
   * is not — the name is what the notice tells a person was about to happen. Absent
   * on a hand-off that a tool call already started, which needs no dispatch because
   * the run is already going.

  directive: string;

   * tool calls, and nothing has to be asked or trusted to tell which.

   * final turn (450 assistant turns with 1 carrying text; 204 with 1; 200 with 0).

   * `post_result_comment.ts` labels one as such when it shows it.
